# Josupeit.Practices.Specifications

> One abstract class, `Specification<TCandidate>`, for named, composable business rules. Override `IsSatisfiedBy(TCandidate)` or `IsSatisfiedByAsync(TCandidate, CancellationToken)` - whichever suits the rule - and the base class bridges the other direction. Compose with the C# operators `&&`/`&`, `||`/`|`, `^`, and `!`; the result is again a `Specification<TCandidate>`, evaluates lazily per candidate, short-circuits, and works in both the synchronous and the asynchronous direction. No expression trees, no lambda factory, no query translation: rules are classes, evaluation is in memory. Targets netstandard2.0 and net8.0; no dependencies; lives in the `Josupeit.Practices.Specifications` namespace.

Install with `dotnet add package Josupeit.Practices.Specifications`. One public type in the `Josupeit.Practices.Specifications` namespace:

- `Specification<TCandidate>` - abstract, protected parameterless constructor; `virtual bool IsSatisfiedBy(TCandidate)`, non-virtual `Task<bool> IsSatisfiedByAsync(TCandidate)` (equals passing `CancellationToken.None`), `virtual Task<bool> IsSatisfiedByAsync(TCandidate, CancellationToken)`; operators `&`, `|`, `^`, `!` returning `Specification<TCandidate>` (`ArgumentNullException` on null), and `true`/`false` both returning `false` so that `&&` and `||` build specifications

Override one direction; the base bridges the other: the asynchronous bridge returns a faulted task instead of throwing and a canceled task for an already-canceled token, the synchronous bridge blocks with `GetAwaiter().GetResult()` and rethrows the original exception. Overriding neither, or calling the base from an override, throws `InvalidOperationException`. `&&`/`&` and `||`/`|` short-circuit at evaluation, `^` evaluates both, `!` negates; composites pass the token down. `if (spec)` compiles and is always `false`. No `And`/`Or` methods, no lambda constructor, no `ToExpression()`, no variance between candidate types.
